I'm not entirely sure where the right discussion for the analytic number theory network is, but this looks like the most appropriate place.

With a lot of AI assistance, I have managed to prove and formalize in Lean some new zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function. Writing N(sigma,T) for the number of nontrivial zeros with real part at least sigma and |Im| <= T, counted with multiplicity, the results include

N(sigma,T) <<_eps T^((39/17)(1-sigma)+eps), uniformly for 1/2 <= sigma <= 1,

and

N(sigma,T) <<_(sigma,eps) T^(3(1-sigma)/(2sigma)+eps), for every fixed 3/4 < sigma < 1.

Both hold for T >= 2 and every eps > 0. The first improves the Guth-Maynard coefficient 30/13 to 39/17, while the second gives the density hypothesis for every fixed sigma > 3/4. There are also sharper piecewise bounds. The attached plot shows how these compare with the earlier estimates.

The formalizations are on GitHub:
https://github.com/mrklwk/zeta-density-39-over-17-lean
https://github.com/mrklwk/zeta-density-three-over-two-sigma-lean

Some of my formalizations are already on Palomar, and the remaining submissions are in progress. There are new large-values estimates underlying these improvements, and I hope to write a traditional paper explaining the arguments. Given how quickly things are moving, though, I thought I would start by making the formalizations available.

This isn't an ideal way to present mathematical work, and I understand there are reasonable criticisms of the approach. It is likely that these bounds will quickly be superseded. Still, I hope putting the formalizations out now is useful, given how many things depend on results of this form. I'd be grateful for comments or corrections.

Thanks Mark, that's great!! Yes, putting them in Palomar is probably the fastest way to disseminate them now. (And of course it would be great to read a paper from you with an explanation of the techniques!)
